methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
JetZero is a Series B-stage frontier transportation company founded by Tom O'Leary and Mark Page that has raised over $1.0B to date. The transportation sector peer set includes eight private companies—notably Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and Parallel Systems—with no public comparables identified. The absence of same-stage or adjacent-stage peers with sufficient data density precluded a reliable peer-median methodology.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology applied to the $1.0B total-raised proxy as the base value. A 1.9x step-up multiplier, consistent with Series B advancement dynamics, yields an implied valuation of $1.9B. This represents the sole triangulation method supported by available data quality thresholds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.6B to $2.2B, centered at $1.9B. The low-end reflects conservative application of the multiplier, while the high-end incorporates reasonable upside variance. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of stage-progression assumptions for frontier transportation subsectors, the absence of narrow peer validation, and the degree to which total raised correlates with fair value at Series B for capital-intensive hardware ventures. A second-stage financing with transparent term sheets or additional comparable company data would materially narrow this range.
